title: text-secondary and text-muted are hard to read
description:
The current text color hierarchy (--text-primary: #f0f0f2, --text-secondary: #9e9eab, --text-muted: #6b6b78) has readability problems. text-secondary is used in 76 places across 16 files and text-muted is even dimmer. Both are hard to read against the dark background, especially for body content.

We should either:
1. Bump the brightness of text-secondary and text-muted so they're more readable at their current usage sites, or
2. Audit all 76+ usages and switch most of them to text-primary, reserving text-secondary/text-muted for genuinely de-emphasized elements like timestamps and token counts.

Probably a mix of both — make the values themselves more readable AND reduce how much we lean on the dimmer tiers for content people actually want to read.
